# Error Handling Checklist: SPEC-014 Control-Flow Graphs

**Purpose**: Validate that SPEC-014 error-handling requirements are complete, precise, consistent, and measurable before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-07-25
**Feature**: ../spec.md

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Expected Absence States

- [x] CHK001 Are disabled, not-indexed, not-computed, unknown-function, deleted, unsupported, resource-limited, unavailable, and stale outcomes defined as expected `CfgReadResult` states rather than thrown read errors? [Completeness, Spec FR-013, Spec FR-028, contracts/cfg-cli.md, contracts/cfg-mcp.md]
- [x] CHK002 Are disabled reads required to consult live config first and return `disabled` without exposing retained rows? [Clarity, Spec FR-002, Spec FR-006, data-model.md]
- [x] CHK003 Are unknown and deleted function IDs differentiated without exposing CFG payloads? [Clarity, Spec FR-005, Spec Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK004 Are all closed error-handling reason codes mapped to their allowed state, payload, and retry/containment outcome? [Completeness, contracts/cfg-shared-contract.md Expected State and Reason Mapping]

## Unsupported And Unsafe Analysis

- [x] CHK005 Are unsupported syntax, unsupported language, parser unavailable, parse errors, and parse-unsafe regions specified as whole-function skips with stable reasons? [Completeness, Spec FR-013, Spec Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK006 Are unsafe constructs required to persist status only and expose no partial CFG blocks or edges? [Acceptance Criteria Quality, Spec FR-016, Spec SC-005, data-model.md]
- [x] CHK007 Is the 10,000-block cap specified as a whole-function `resource_limited` skip with stable `block_limit_exceeded` reason and no partial payload? [Clarity, Spec FR-017, Plan Performance and Reliability]
- [x] CHK008 Is stale retention explicitly excluded when a previously supported function becomes unsupported or resource-limited on refresh? [Consistency, data-model.md State Transitions]

## Exception Semantics

- [x] CHK009 Are exception-control requirements limited to explicit TypeScript/JavaScript `throw` and Python `raise` syntax? [Clarity, Spec FR-018, data-model.md]
- [x] CHK010 Are implicit exception edges from calls, property access, allocation, or other potentially failing operations explicitly excluded? [Completeness, Spec FR-018, Plan Constraints]
- [x] CHK011 Are `try`/`finally` normal and abrupt transfer rules specified without collapsing semantically distinct edge kinds? [Clarity, Spec FR-018, Spec FR-027]

## Refresh Failures And Cancellation

- [x] CHK012 Are unexpected first-run refresh failures differentiated from later failures with prior snapshots? [Completeness, Spec FR-008, Spec FR-009, data-model.md State Transitions]
- [x] CHK013 Are later refresh failures required to retain only an explicitly stale prior snapshot with stable `refresh_failed_retained_stale` reason? [Clarity, Spec FR-008, data-model.md]
- [x] CHK014 Are first-run failures required to return `unavailable` with `first_refresh_failed` and no CFG payload? [Clarity, Spec FR-009, data-model.md]
- [x] CHK015 Are cancellation semantics defined as no marker/no partial writes before swap and committed-result-stands after swap? [Acceptance Criteria Quality, Spec FR-009, data-model.md]

## Containment And Safe Diagnostics

- [x] CHK016 Are unexpected CFG analysis failures explicitly contained so ordinary indexing/sync can still complete without publishing partial CFG state? [Completeness, Spec FR-009, Plan Persistence and Lifecycle]
- [x] CHK017 Are safe diagnostic message requirements bounded to 240 Unicode code points and free of raw source text or raw exception strings? [Measurability, Spec FR-013, contracts/cfg-shared-contract.md]
- [x] CHK018 Are CLI and MCP error boundaries clear that expected CFG states are success-shaped while invalid usage, access refusals, serialization/output failure, or real malfunctions may fail? [Consistency, Spec FR-028, contracts/cfg-cli.md, contracts/cfg-mcp.md]

## Verification Coverage

- [x] CHK019 Are lifecycle tests required to cover stale failure, first failure, cancellation, disable, delete, and re-enable with real SQLite? [Coverage, Spec SC-004, Plan Slice 1 Verification Gates]
- [x] CHK020 Are success criteria measurable for stable skip reasons and zero partial block/edge payloads across unsupported, parse-unsafe, and over-limit fixtures? [Measurability, Spec SC-005]
